blocks.text: 5.3 Equations of Medians, Altitudes and Right Bisectors

blocks.prompt: 21 Triangle \(ABC\) has vertices \(A(-2, 1)\), \(B(4, 3)\), \(C(2, -5)\). Find the equation of the median through \(A\).

book_ref.quote: A median joins the vertex of a triangle to the mid-point of the opposite side.

blocks.prompt: 22 For the triangle \(A(-2, 1)\), \(B(4, 3)\), \(C(2, -5)\), find the altitude through \(B\).
blocks.explanation: Slope of \(CA = \dfrac{1 + 5}{-2 - 2} = -\dfrac{3}{2}\), so the altitude has slope \(\dfrac{2}{3}\): \(y - 3 = \dfrac{2}{3}(x - 4) \Rightarrow 2x - 3y + 1 = 0\).

book_ref.quote: An altitude is the line drawn from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

blocks.prompt: 23 For the triangle \(A(-2, 1)\), \(B(4, 3)\), \(C(2, -5)\), find the right bisector of \(\overline{AB}\).
blocks.explanation: Mid-point of \(AB\): \((1, 2)\); slope of \(AB = \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{1}{3}\), perpendicular slope \(-3\): \(y - 2 = -3(x - 1) \Rightarrow 3x + y - 5 = 0\).

book_ref.quote: A perpendicular or right bisector of a triangle is a line that is perpendicular to one side of the triangle

blocks.text: 5.4 Condition of Concurrency of Three Straight Lines

blocks.prompt: 26 State Theorem 3 (condition of concurrency of three lines).
blocks.explanation: Three non-parallel lines \(a_ix + b_iy + c_i = 0\) (\(i = 1, 2, 3\)) are concurrent iff \(\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\).

book_ref.quote: Theorem 3: three non-parallel lines

blocks.text: 5.8 Homogeneous Equation of the Second Degree in Two Variables

blocks.prompt: 46 What is a joint equation? Find the joint equation of \(x - 4y = 0\) and \(2x + y = 0\).
blocks.explanation: The product of the equations of two lines, set equal to zero, is their joint equation. \((x - 4y)(2x + y) = 2x^{2} + xy - 8xy - 4y^{2} = 0\), i.e. \(2x^{2} - 7xy - 4y^{2} = 0\).

book_ref.quote: is called joint equation of the pair of lines (i) and (ii)

blocks.prompt: 47 Find the joint equation of the lines through the origin with slopes \(2\) and \(-\dfrac{1}{2}\).

book_ref.quote: Equation (v) is a special type of a second degree homogeneous equation.

blocks.prompt: 48 Is \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 9 = 0\) a pair of lines? Give a reason.
blocks.explanation: No. It is the circle of radius \(3\) about the origin. A second degree equation is a pair of lines only if it splits into two linear factors, and \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 9\) has no such real factors.

book_ref.quote: is a circle; it cannot be split into two linear factors with real coefficients

blocks.prompt: 49 Define a homogeneous equation of degree \(n\). Show that \(x^{2} - 3xy + 2y^{2} = 0\) is homogeneous of degree \(2\).
blocks.explanation: \(f(x, y) = 0\) is homogeneous of degree \(n\) if \(f(kx, ky) = k^{n}f(x, y)\) for every real \(k\). Here \(f(kx, ky) = k^{2}x^{2} - 3k^{2}xy + 2k^{2}y^{2} = k^{2}f(x, y)\): degree \(2\).

book_ref.quote: This happens exactly when every term has the same total degree
